title: Edge capacity forecast cribsheet - 2026-12-10
body:
Purpose:
Quick cribsheet for the week: short summary of signals, experiments, and actions for edge GPU capacity (APAC + US-west primarily). Use as meeting primer for on-call + surge squad. Not a final runbook — notes, ideas, TODOs.

Attendees:
- Maya Patel (owner)
- Julian Park (fleet ops)
- Lena Ortiz (SRE - priming)
- Ravi Shah (capacity planning)
- Hannah Lee (observability)

TL;DR (1-2 lines):
- APAC edge observed 18% tail-latency increase at p99.9 during 09:30-10:20 UTC on 2026-12-09; correlated to large sequence-length spikes from a single tenant batch.
- Prewarming experiment #E22 reduced cold-start rate by ~67% but increased transient queueing for small-model routing. Need routing tweak.
- Recommend bumping regional buffer for APAC by +10% for next 72h and running targeted priming for high-LL seq clients.

Quick signals snapshot (as observed in dashboards):
- p50/p90/p99 token latency (US-west): 12ms / 28ms / 120ms.
- APAC p99.9: 480ms -> baseline 410ms (spike window).
- Cold-start count (edge nodes): 42 -> after E22: 14.
- Queue depth variance correlates with model-size-mix shifts (large model kernel swaps).

What happened (incident sketch):
- 09:15 UTC - increased request mix for long-sequence generation from partner X (unknown prompt set).
- 09:30 UTC - autoscaler triggered new nodes but they land with cold model caches; traffic backfills to a few hot nodes, hitting KV/cache eviction thrash and pushing p99.9 up.
- 09:45-10:10 UTC - fallback routing kicked in for some classes, but not all because of route-policy mismatches between hosted/dedicated clusters.
- 10:20 UTC - partner throttled and latency recovered.

Notes-to-self / open questions:
- Why did autoscaler pick instance types with slower NVLink for this wave? check provisioning logs + instance selection policy.
- Should we add a policy: for sequences >8k prefer pre-warmed large-kernel pool? (sketch below)
- Can opt-in tenants mark traffic as "long-context-heavy" to get pinned lanes? (product/solutions ask)

Experiment summary: prewarming E22 (last 7 days) - design: proactive model load + incremental KV priming on warm nodes, TTL 3h. - results: cold-starts drop 67%; average token-cost +-2%; small-model route latency increased 8% during peak overlaps. - notes: collision between prewarm and small-model burst - priming steals GPU mem and leads to kernel-selection path change.

Conclusions from E22:
- prewarm helps large-context clients strongly; needs smarter memory-guard (evictable slots reserved) so small-model latency doesn't regress.
- propose memory-guard prototype: reserve 8GB for small-model lanes per GPU (heuristic) — see linked PR.

Immediate recommendations (72h):
- Increase APAC buffer pool by +10% (Ravi) - JIRA-1729 to track.
- Roll E22 to staggered schedule: only run prewarm on nodes flagged as "low-priority-burst" between 02:00-08:00 local (Julian / ops).
- Add quick patch to router to prefer placing long-context requests to prewarm-enabled nodes when available (PR referenced).
- Add trace tag 'seq-len-bucket' to logs to catch noisy tenants (Hannah).

Routing + autoscaler ideas (brainstorm):
- Latency anchoring: maintain a small pool of "latency-anchors" (hot nodes with pinned small-model kernels) per region to guarantee p50/p90 even during priming.
- Heuristic: if seq_len > 4096 route to node pool A; else pool B. Needs fallthrough to avoid starvation.
- Autoscaler: weigh instance selection by historical NVLink score (collect performance histogram per instance-type).

Playbook snippet (for oncall):
- If p99.9 > 450ms for >15m in region X:
  1) Flip route-weight to favor latency-anchor pool (manual toggle in console).
  2) If cold-start rate > 30/min and priming jobs running, pause priming.
  3) Open JIRA incident 'edge-latency-<region>-<date>' and assign to ops lead.
  4) Run quick node-evac script to reduce KV eviction thrash (link in Confluence page).

Action items (owners):
- Ravi: implement APAC +10% buffer bump (JIRA-1729). due 2026-12-12.
- Julian: staggered E22 rollout plan + ops-side toggle. add note on console toggles. due 2026-12-12.
- Hannah: instrument seq-len-bucket traces and add dashboard tile. due 2026-12-13.
- Maya: prototype memory-guard JIT heuristic and open follow-up PR. due 2026-12-15.
- Lena: validate autoscaler instance-selection logs and attach histogram to JIRA-1934. due 2026-12-13.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: buffer bump increases reserved idle spend by ~8-12% regionally. Mitigation: set auto-scale-down threshold to more aggressive after 72h and review usage.
- Risk: priming pause may cause cold-starts for some premium customers. Mitigation: maintain a small pinned lane for premium tenants.

Unresolved design decisions (for next architecture sync):
- Global policy for long-context routing (binary vs. probabilistic steering).
- Whether tenants can opt-in to pinned lanes (billing/SLAs implications).

Meeting follow-ups / syncs scheduled:
- Ops sync: 2026-12-11 08:00 UTC (check APAC buffer bump progress).
- Architecture sync: 2026-12-14 16:00 UTC (memory-guard design review).

Random notes & scribbles:
- Might be worth sampling payloads (anonymized) from partner X to classify prompt patterns — legal ok? RSVP legal.
- Consider a short paper on "edge latency anchors" for internal knowledge base.
- TODO: add cost-sensitivity calc for bumping buffers (Ravi).

References (links copied):
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EDGE/Priming+Playbook
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-scripts/pull/421
- Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/JIRA-1729

End of cribsheet.

(half-formed ideas kept intentionally casual. this lives in Drive as working notes — update and formalize if we converge.)
